query.label: Filter query

help.intro: To filter tasks, you can use a query syntax similar to SQL. The available fields for filtering include:
help.canUseDatemath: You can use date math to set relative dates. Click on the date value in a query to find out more.

fields.done: Whether the task is completed or not
fields.priority: The priority level of the task (1-5)
fields.percentDone: The percentage of completion for the task (0-100)
fields.dueDate: The due date of the task
fields.startDate: The start date of the task
fields.endDate: The end date of the task
fields.doneAt: The date and time when the task was completed
fields.createdBy: The user who created the task (matched by username)
fields.labels: The labels associated with the task
fields.project: The project the task belongs to (only available for saved filters, not on a project level)
fields.reminders: The reminders of the task as a date field, will return all tasks with at least one reminder matching the query
fields.created: The time and date when the task was created
fields.updated: The time and date when the task was last changed

operators.intro: The available operators for filtering include:
operators.in: Matches any value in a comma-separated list of values
operators.notIn: Matches any value not present in a comma-separated list of values

logicalOperators.intro: To combine multiple conditions, you can use the following logical operators:
logicalOperators.and: AND operator, matches if all conditions are true
logicalOperators.or: OR operator, matches if any of the conditions are true

examples.intro: Here are some examples of filter queries:
examples.dueDatePast: Matches tasks with a due date in the past
examples.undoneHighPriority: Matches undone tasks with priority level 3 or higher
examples.assigneesIn: Matches tasks assigned to either "user1" or "user2"
examples.priorityOneOrTwoPastDue: Matches tasks with priority level 1 or 2 and a due date in the past

quickAddMagic.title: Quick Add Magic
quickAddMagic.intro: When creating a task, you can use special keywords to directly add attributes to the newly created task. This allows to add commonly used attributes to tasks much faster.
quickAddMagic.multiple: You can use this multiple times.
quickAddMagic.label1: To add a label, simply prefix the name of the label with {prefix}.
quickAddMagic.label2: Vikunja will first check if the label already exist and create it if not.
quickAddMagic.label3: To use spaces, simply add a " or ' around the label name.
quickAddMagic.priority1: To set a task's priority, add a number 1-5, prefixed with a {prefix}.
quickAddMagic.priority2: The higher the number, the higher the priority.
quickAddMagic.assignees: To directly assign the task to a user, add their username prefixed with {prefix} to the task.
quickAddMagic.project1: To set a project for the task to appear in, enter its name prefixed with {prefix}.
quickAddMagic.project2: This will return an error if the project does not exist.
quickAddMagic.project3: To use spaces, simply add a " or ' around the project name.
quickAddMagic.date: Any date will be used as the due date of the new task. You can use dates in any of these formats:
quickAddMagic.dateWeekday: any weekday, will use the next date with that day
quickAddMagic.dateNth: will use the {day}th of the current month
quickAddMagic.dateTime: Combine any of the date formats with "{time}" (or {timePM}) to set a time.
quickAddMagic.repeatsDescription: To set a task as repeating in an interval, simply add '{suffix}' to the task text. The amount needs to be a number and can be omitted to use just the type (see examples).

tour.welcomeText: Explore tasks, AI, voice and your public page.
tour.title: What would you like to explore?
tour.description: Choose a tour to visit its pages and highlight their controls. Tours explain the interface; you decide when to save, send or publish. Finish unsaved edits before starting.
tour.remembered: This browser remembers completed tours separately for each account. Open this menu anytime to replay them.
tour.missing: This area is unavailable or could not finish loading. Continue, or close the guide and try again later.
tour.locating: Opening the page and locating this area…

basics.title: Everyday tasks
basics.description: Navigate, add tasks, plan your time and collaborate.

ai.title: AI & voice
ai.description: Connect models, assign their roles and use the assistant.

showcase.title: Your public page
showcase.description: Choose what to share, preview it and publish when ready.

overview.title: Your starting point
overview.text: The overview brings your tasks and recently visited projects together. Use the sidebar to explore your workspace. On phones, the guide opens the sidebar when needed.

projects.title: Organize work into projects
projects.text: Create a project here, then add its tasks. Projects support list, kanban, table and Gantt views so you can organize the same work in different ways.

addTask.title: Add a task quickly
addTask.text: Type a task here and choose its project when asked. Open a task to add details, priority, reminders, assignees and dates. The guide will not create a sample task.

upcoming.title: Plan dates and time slots
upcoming.text: Upcoming shows tasks by date. Set a due date for a deadline, or start and end times for a time slot. Use a project’s Gantt view to see how scheduled tasks fit together.

teams.title: Work with other accounts
teams.text: Create teams and add members here. Share projects with users or teams from project settings, with read, write or admin access. Shared tasks support assignees and comments.

search.title: Find things quickly
search.text: Use search to find tasks or projects and run quick actions. Press Ctrl+K on Windows/Linux or Command+K on macOS.

assistant.title: Turn words into a plan
assistant.text: The assistant accepts text and audio. First connect your models in Settings → AI & voice. It can look up accessible tasks or make changes according to your chosen mode.

settings.title: Your account and preferences
settings.text: Open the avatar menu for settings. AI & voice connects your models; Public page shares selected schedules with aliases and privacy rules. Private projects are not automatically public.

replay.title: Help is always here
replay.text: Click the question mark or choose Help & guided tours in the avatar menu to replay a tour. Use Back/Next or the left/right arrow keys to change steps. Escape closes the guide.

connections.title: Connect your model provider
connections.text: Configure your provider’s API base URL, key, model ID and protocol here. Include its required version path. The form shows full request and model-list endpoints for troubleshooting.

addConnection.title: Add and test a connection
addConnection.text: Add a connection here. Text supports OpenAI Chat/Responses, Anthropic and Gemini; speech supports OpenAI Transcriptions, OpenAI Chat Audio and Gemini. Fetch models or enter an ID manually, then save before testing.

roles.title: Choose a model for each job
roles.text: Assign separate models to the task assistant, speech recognition and transcript cleanup. The assistant needs tool calling; speech needs audio input. Each role can use a different provider.

saveModels.title: Save, then test
saveModels.text: Save connections and role assignments here. Leave an existing key blank to keep it. Use each connection’s test button after saving. This guide does not save settings or contact your provider.

permissions.title: Choose what AI may do
permissions.text: Expand model, project and permissions to choose a project. Start in read-only mode to check results, then allow changes only when needed. Deletion requires a separate switch.

voice.title: Speak, review, then send
voice.text: Record or upload audio after assigning a speech model. Optionally clean up the transcript, review and edit it, then send it yourself. Recording needs microphone permission; the guide never turns it on.

send.title: Describe the result you want
send.text: Write or review your request here, then send it yourself. Check the operation history and resulting tasks. If a request fails, some earlier operations may already have succeeded.

publication.title: A separate page for visitors
publication.text: Check whether your page is published. After publishing, open the public webpage or JSON endpoint for bots here, or take both down. Visitors do not need an account.

hours.title: Set the public time window
hours.text: Set your page address, title, days and available hours. Tasks with start and end times form busy slots; deadlines do not occupy the whole day. Public calculations use Asia/Shanghai time.

privacy.title: Choose what others may see
privacy.text: Only projects added here appear publicly. Show busy times without names, allow titles with aliases, or hide a project completely. Preview first to alias or hide individual tasks. Private names stay unchanged.

customPage.title: Make the page your own
customPage.text: Write Markdown or static HTML. Insert schedules, availability and projects using the template button. A custom body can replace the default panels. Hiding panels does not change the public JSON’s data scope.

preview.title: Preview before publishing
preview.text: Preview shows the visitor-facing result without publishing it. Review names, hidden tasks and time slots. After editing, preview again before publishing. The guide does not preview or change your draft.

publish.title: Publish only when ready
publish.text: Saving a draft keeps it private. Publish this preview updates the webpage and JSON. Published schedules follow live tasks using the last published rules. Hidden or unselected tasks do not count as busy, so public free time may differ from your full calendar.

chat.noConversations: Your saved conversations will appear here.
chat.savedOnServer: Private to your account. Conversations and model context are encrypted on this server.
chat.loadFailed: This conversation could not be loaded.
chat.originalsPreserved: Original messages are kept. The checkpoint covers the entire conversation through the recorded turn; subsequent requests use it and any new messages.
chat.enterHint: Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line
chat.promptNote: This is the current system prompt. Each message also includes saved conversation context and your request. Its actual prompt is saved with the response.
chat.sendFailed: The message could not be sent. Your draft has been kept.
chat.deleteConfirm: Delete this conversation and its saved model context? This does not delete tasks or projects.
chat.forkConfirm: Create a new conversation through this response? Existing task and project changes remain in place; branching does not undo or replay them.
chat.compactConfirm: Create a handoff checkpoint from the entire current conversation, including real tool outcomes? Original messages are kept. This consumes model tokens and continues in the background when you leave the page.
chat.noReasoning: The provider did not return visible thinking for this round.
chat.interrupted: The server restarted during this run. Operations will not be replayed automatically. Check the saved results before continuing.
chat.stopped: Execution stopped. Completed operations remain in place.
chat.requestDetails: Request details and actual system prompt
chat.metricNotes: Usage is reported by the provider and summed across model rounds. Cached and reasoning tokens are included in input/output totals. First token measures the first streamed text or thinking chunk; first answer text excludes thinking. If no streaming evidence or usage is returned, the metric is not provided.
chat.partialUsage: Some rounds did not report usage; these totals are partial.

debug.title: Errors and diagnostics
debug.description: Inspect recent request errors and agent runs. Reports are generated in this browser and never sent automatically; reloading clears this list.
debug.empty: No errors recorded. You can still download the current environment information.
debug.includeDetails: Include error details, tool arguments and results (may contain private content)
debug.privacy: Conversation text, tool arguments and results are excluded by default. If enabled, inspect the preview before sharing: credential fields are redacted, but free text may still contain private information. Request headers, login tokens and raw audio are never collected.
debug.proxyError: A proxy or protection page blocked this request. Open Errors and diagnostics to inspect the HTTP status and request endpoint.

agent.reviewDescription: These are the current records read by the server and the exact proposed changes. Approval applies only to this preview; changed records require a fresh review.
agent.invalidJSON: Enter a valid JSON object. Updating a preview does not execute it.
agent.questionTitle: A little more information is needed
agent.budgetExplanation: Completed operations are retained. Continuing grants another segment of the same budget and resumes saved state without replaying completed tools.
agent.smart: Smart: review bulk, destructive and notification actions
agent.auto: Autonomous: run bulk writes; still review destructive and notification actions
agent.writeScope: Allow writes only to these projects (multiple selection)
agent.scopeHelp: An empty selection follows your existing account permissions. The current project is context only. With a scope selected, writes outside it and creating projects are rejected.
agent.tokenLimit: Soft token limit per segment (0 disables)
agent.tokenHelp: Checked between requests using provider-reported usage. A single request may exceed the limit; unreported usage cannot be counted.
agent.waitingReview: This turn is paused. Use its operation card above, or stop this turn before sending a new message.
agent.fromTask: Work on this task with AI
agent.overallLimit: The overall ceiling of 200 rounds or 1000 operations has been reached. Stop this turn and inspect completed records before starting a new request.

flow.cropAvatar: Crop to a square before choosing the upload format (changes the original image)
flow.imageNote: Choose for this upload. Original keeps the selected file; avatar cropping and display thumbnails remain separate.
flow.animationKept: Animated images, SVG and formats the browser cannot convert are uploaded unchanged. WebP conversion is available for JPEG, PNG, WebP and BMP.
flow.imageFailed: The browser could not convert this image to WebP. Try the original file.
flow.processing: Upload received; server is validating and saving…
flow.nonStreaming: Use non-streaming responses (streaming is enabled by default)
flow.compacting: Compacting the entire conversation in the background…
flow.compactFailed: Compaction did not finish; the previous checkpoint is preserved.
flow.reconnecting: Connecting to live events; polling remains available
flow.backgroundNote: Leaving this page keeps the server job running
flow.observedCharacters: {count} visible characters received · not a token estimate
flow.stage_review: Waiting for your review or answer
flow.taskInvite: Type a task title here, then press Enter or choose Add.
flow.coverNote: This image is both the project background and its cover on project cards. Choose a file to preview its format options before upload.
flow.streamIgnored: Streaming was requested, but the provider returned a complete response.
